findings.title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The dataclass field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, so timezone.now() runs once when the class is defined rather than for each AssignmentSource. Every instance created without an explicit queued value therefore shares the process import time, making queued incorrect as a record of when an assignment was queued. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) instead.

findings.title: to_dict produces a non-JSON-serializable Celery argument and breaks round-trip typing
findings.body: to_dict() uses asdict(), leaving queued as a datetime object. sync_group_assignee_outbound puts this dict directly into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async kwargs, which must cross Sentry's task serialization boundary; a datetime is not a plain JSON value, and if encoded as an ISO string, from_dict will construct an AssignmentSource whose queued field is a string rather than a datetime. Serialize queued explicitly (for example as an ISO timestamp) and parse it back in from_dict so the round trip is safe and type-consistent.

findings.title: Outbound suppression is only tested for assignment, not deassignment or other integrations
findings.body: The new matching-source test covers only GroupAssignee.assign. The deassign suppression uses separate branches in GroupAssignee.deassign and in sync_group_assignee_inbound's assign=False path, so a regression there would still echo unassignments back to the originating integration and would not be caught. There is also no test that an assignment sourced from one integration still syncs to a different linked integration, so over-suppression would not be caught either.
